license.date: circa 1947 date QS:P,+1947-00-00T00:00:00Z/9,P1480,Q5727902 , when Fletcher made a recording of his routine "Open the Door, Richard" for National Records, and 1954 (his death). The record went to #3 on Billboard' s charts in 1947. Fletcher's fame grew when National Records helped him sue Jack McVea for using Fletcher's material as the basis of the song, recording it and having a hit with it in 1946. Because of the suit, Fletcher was given credit as being one of the authors of the song.
